lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs finally found a foothold on the road, and now the burden is to prove it was more than a brief correction. Saturday's 4-2 victory over Vancouver pushed Toronto to 8-6, a one-game winning streak and 18 points - good for fifth in the Eastern Conference, five points off the pace. Auston Matthews supplied the familiar engine, scoring his team-leading 11th goal, while William Nylander arrives in dangerous form with five goals and five assists over his last 10 games. The lineup, however, remains a moving target: Easton Cowan has been reunited with Matthews and Jack Roslovic, while injuries continue to sideline John Tavares, Kirill Marchenko and Max Domi. Sergei Bobrovsky gets the crease again despite a difficult opening month. That is a gamble, not a coronation. Tonight's Mammoth test at 7 p.m. ET begins a six-game homestand - watch whether Cowan's promotion and Bobrovsky's rebound can turn a .500-ish start into a climb.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season is over, and Toronto's first move has already drawn the line: the Blue Jays declined Myles Straw's $8 million option, paying a $1.75 million buyout while opening a roster spot and a month of decisions. That is not a teardown; it is a declaration that competent depth cannot be allowed to masquerade as a finished outfield. After a 79-83 finish in second place in the AL East, the Jays need more than cosmetic repairs. Dylan Cease gives the winter a genuine headline - he is an AL Cy Young finalist - while Louis Varland's Reliever of the Year nomination confirms the bullpen has a cornerstone, not merely a collection of arms. The challenge is converting those bright spots into a sturdier roster, particularly around the lineup and bench. Watch the 40-man churn, the arbitration tender deadline on November 20, and whether Toronto turns Straw's departure into an upgrade rather than a vacancy.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: A season that looked ready to wobble instead found a pulse in the fourth quarter. Toronto erased a 12-point deficit to beat the Clippers 125-118, turning a grim night into a road win and a one-game streak. Scottie Barnes supplied the jolt, scoring 15 of his 22 points in the final period, while Immanuel Quickley's 27 points and RJ Barrett's 26 steadied the attack. That matters for a club now 4-3, third in the Atlantic Division - respectable, but hardly secure after losses to the Lakers and Magic. The larger concern remains Kawhi Leonard, whose knee swelling has kept him out and postponed his return to Los Angeles; Jakob Poeltl also missed his second straight game. This team can survive absences, not indefinitely. Denver is next Wednesday at 9 p.m. ET - a sharp test of whether Monday's rally was resilience or rescue.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The Commanders nearly handed the Eagles a 10-point head start, then remembered who they could be. Washington's 27-10 victory over Philadelphia was a needed jolt - 27 unanswered points, a defense that produced five sacks, and Jayden Daniels pulling the offense together when it threatened to drift. Daniels finished with 217 passing yards and a touchdown, adding 23 yards on the ground, but the pre-snap penalties remain an irritating, self-inflicted tax. At 2-4-1, Washington sits second in the NFC East, two games behind the Giants, with a one-game winning streak and, at last, a little breathing room. The price was steep: Jeremy McNichols suffered a concerning midfoot injury and could miss extended time, thinning a backfield already short on depth. Sunday's visit from the Rams at 1 p.m. ET will test whether this was a revival or merely a reprieve.

article.title: Raptors Rally Past Clippers in Fourth Quarter
paragraphs: The Raptors rallied past the Clippers 125-118 on Monday, improving to 4-3. Immanuel Quickley scored 27 points, while Scottie Barnes added 15 rebounds and eight assists. Toronto now visits Denver on Wednesday at 9:00 PM ET.

The Leafs host the Mammoth tonight at 7:00 PM ET on TSN, with Sergei Bobrovsky confirmed to face Karel Vejmelka. Toronto is 8-6 and fifth in the Eastern Conference, while coach Jim Hiller has reunited Nick Robertson and Auston Matthews on the shuffled lines. The Jays are looking ahead to a busy offseason after declining Myles Straw's option, with Monday's deadline decisions shaping the month ahead.

The Commanders, 2-4-1 and second in the NFC East, host the Rams on Sunday at 1:00 PM ET on Fox. Pre-snap penalties remain a central concern before that game. For tonight, Bobrovsky's record is 3-5-2 with a 3.28 goals-against average.
